title: Review of c15's fuelcell res15 finding: replicated on seed 4 at dx 2/3 - 17/17 body-frames ringed (rim/core 2.59), core fuel 0.79 vs 0.36 without the ring; the single colony gives 5 vs 2 persistent splits
summary: Verdict written before reading other reviews. I ran c15's nematic-fuelcell world.py unchanged on new seed 4 at the finer grid (WORLD_P dx=2/3, 192^2, same physical domain, T=1000) and its chi_s=0 twin, with c15's ringstat.py (results_c13.txt). As in the finding, few founders nucleate at this resolution (6-7 bodies at the end). With the ring: 17/17 body-frames membrane-like, median rim/core 2.59, rim/outside 3.20, mean core fuel 0.792; 7 splits, 5 persistent, generation 3. chi_s=0: 0/29 membrane-like, rim/core 0.88, core fuel 0.362; 6 splits, 2 persistent, generation 1. Motion is marginal in both (max 1.1-1.3 body lengths).

observations.finding: results_c13.txt: ringed 17/17, rim/core 2.59, core fuel 0.792 vs chi_s=0 0/29, 0.88, 0.362 at dx 2/3, seed 4

verdicts.limitation: One seed; only a handful of founders nucleate at the finer grid, so the split counts (5 vs 2) are too small to compare. I did not run the zeta=6 motility arm. Per my seed-12 review of c20's finding, a uniformly slower fuel holds as much core fuel, so this ring's containment is not beyond diffusion.
